newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gaddum - Germany to issue more strippable bonds.
newsitem.headline: Gaddum - Germany to issue more strippable bonds.

text.p: Bundesbank deputy president Johann Gaddum said on Tuesday that the total volume of strippable German government bonds was now 77 billion marks.

Gaddum, who was speaking at a news conference called to announce the issuance of a new strippable 30-year bond, also said the Bonn government intended to issue more strippable bonds or add to existed issues with strippable paper.
Juergen Stark, state secretary in the German finance ministry, also told the news conference that Germany planned gradually to offer stripping of government debt across the full maturity curve.
The Bundesbank said earlier on Tuesday that it had sold 3.0 billion marks of the Bonn government's new 6.5 percent coupon 30-year bond via a consortium of banks.
The bond, sold at 99.75, had a yield of 6.52 percent, the Bundesbank said.
